title: Finite recoverability-first projected Petz transport
question: Can approximate Markovness of a low-energy projected Gibbs state be transported back to the original state with a dimension-free Petz triangle and contractivity budget, avoiding a dimension-growing entropy-continuity shortcut?
method: Build the finite Q3LOCK Gibbs state on every declared volume and oscillator cutoff, and enumerate both orientations, core widths, buffer widths, beta values and energy windows.
Project the local A core, normalize the projected state, and build one Petz map from its BC and B marginals; apply the same map to the original AB reduction.
Check projected and transported trace distances, partial-trace contractivity, recovered-state positivity and the triangle budget with both displacement terms.
Retain per-cutoff transport profiles and adjacent ratios so finite recovery success cannot hide regulator growth.
Rebuild the full table without importing the primary module, run an omitted-displacement hostile mutation, and compile the scalar Lean triangle and contractivity skeleton.
finding: The primary lane passes 5961/5961 assertions over 12 volume/cutoff systems, 62 tripartitions and 992 rows. The non-importing independent lane passes 6/6 aggregate checks, the hostile lane passes 3/3 and the integrated verifier passes 23/23 with Lean R396. The maximum projected recovery error is 0.0246593411003531, transported error 0.0260340558191261, triangle budget 1.67739253805716 and contractivity gap 6.68182482377048e-16. All finite violation counts are zero, but the adjacent-cutoff transport ratio reaches 6.91143733666218.
decision_reason: R-396 supplies a distinct finite approximate-Markov transport interface: it keeps the recovery map fixed and replaces a dimension-growing entropy-continuity shortcut by contractivity plus a transparent triangle budget. The finite cutoff profile remains nonuniform, so this advances only the interface and identifies the next need for a dimension-safe continuity or moment theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite projected-state transport only. It proves no dimension-safe QCMI upper bound, cutoff/source/volume/shape uniformity, Gibbs moment theorem, shell summability, common form core, Cook/common-alpha convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
next_action: Test a semigroup-dressed smooth spectral collar that removes hard projector rank jumps, while keeping the R-396 fixed-reference Petz and displacement accounting. Require a finite primary/independent/hostile/Lean package and retire the route if its normalized disturbance still grows under every declared collar scaling.

adversarial_review.check: The projected BC and B marginals define one recovery map that is reused for both projected and original inputs.
Recovered input distance is checked against AB distance and AB distance against ABC distance on every row.
Both ABC and AB displacement terms are retained and a second two-ABC envelope is checked.
Recovered traces and minimum eigenvalues are checked without hiding a negative eigenvalue by clipping.
Dropping both displacement terms is separated on the hostile row and is rejected.
The adjacent transport ratio reaches 6.91143733666218, so no cutoff-independent continuity is inferred.
Moment, shell, common-core, common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A obligations remain open.
